claims.text: All four witnesses narrate sentencing, execution, death, and burial while selecting different hearings, sayings, time notices, signs, people, and bodily details.
The sources name rulers, crowds, Pilate, lawless hands, God’s plan, raising, witness, and prophetic announcement in distinct clauses.
Questions, robes, thorns, salutes, political pressure, inscriptions, and public reading repeatedly place royal language around humiliation and execution.
The Crucifixion witness takes up cry, garments, thirst, unbroken-bone, and piercing language while retaining eyewitness and bodily sequence.
The witnesses preserve lament, forgiveness, promise, thirst, completion, and entrusting speech in their own narrated settings.
The burial accounts name requests, official confirmation, body preparation, linen, spices, tomb locations, women witnesses, Sabbath timing, a seal, and a guard in differing combinations.
The proclaimed event remains death and divine raising while the immediate evidence shifts among deeds, Scripture, healing, witnesses, forgiveness, and audience responsibility.
Later passages carry the Crucifixion into distinct arguments about communal identity, peace, priestly offering, conduct under suffering, and the Lamb’s worthiness.
